pr_comments: Frankly speaking, I treat the commented out `__owur`s as a bug, though I am ready to adjust the checks to make Coverity happy.

> Frankly speaking, I treat the commented out `__owur`s as a bug, though I am ready to adjust the checks to make Coverity happy.

It will be quite hard not to introduce additional warnings on modern compilers unless you really add proper error checking in speed. Is that something that should go in 3.0? Not sure, IMO rather not.

Currently my practice show that at least `Init` functions should be `__owur`-ed. If their result is not checked for the unavailable algorithms, the crash occurs when `Update` is called. So I'd like at least to enforce these checks.

We can discuss this going into 3.0 at the OTC call.
Post 3.0, I think it should go in.
OTC voted against including this in 3.0. I guess there's no reason it can't be merged post 3.0.

One of the reasons is because __owur is defined to be empty unless --strict-warnings is used which applies only to compiling openssl itself and thus it does not really affect external users. They would have to define UNUSEDRESULT_DEBUG.

issue_context.title: __owur question
issue_context.body:
Some functions from the OpenSSL public API have an `__owur` attribute that raises a warning when its result is not checked.

This warning is guarded by `-DUNUSEDRESULT_DEBUG` define.

I wonder why, e.g. `EVP_EncryptInit` has such an attribute while `EVP_EncryptInit_ex` doesn't. It looks suspicious to me. 
Also I'd like to rename the `-DUNUSEDRESULT_DEBUG` to `-DOPENSSL_UNUSEDRESULT_DEBUG`.
comments: These seem to me like possible Post 3.0 changes.
I understand your reasons but I have my own at least to uncomment the commented ones and see what happens...
The necessary changes looks pretty small. All the unchecked values are found only in apps.
I suspect that quite a number of user applications don't check the return.  Making this change will break them.

And because they don't check the returns they are affected by the introduction of the legacy provider.
They're using the OpenSSL API incorrectly, why we should accommodate them?

> I suspect that quite a number of user applications don't check the return. Making this change will break them.

Let me disagree.

1. They have to check it to avoid being crashed
2. It is a compile-time check and to enable this check they need to add special compile-time settings

> I suspect that quite a number of user applications don't check the return. Making this change will break them.

Unlikely. The check only occurs if the application explicitly defines `UNUSEDRESULT_DEBUG`. We do this for our own code (if you pass `--strict-warnings`) - but my guess is most applications don't do this. And if they do they are probably interested in this kind of failure.
I suspect the --strict-warnings option is used commonly.  Perhaps errantly...

Anyway it doesn't raise any errors for the external application without the #define.

@paulidale, the results are available in #15902. Would you mind to review?

This is #15902....
I'm off to sleep now.

> I suspect the --strict-warnings option is used commonly

That doesn't matter. `--strict-warnings` is only relevant for compiling our own code. It adds the `UNUSEDRESULT_DEBUG` define when building OpenSSL. But we regularly test that so it is fine. External applications would have to explicitly define `UNUSEDRESULT_DEBUG` in some other way (which I guess most do not).
As per my comment in #15905, this is now a post 3.0 thing. Removing OTC hold.
